newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia looks to limit arms export licences.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia looks to limit arms export licences.

text.p: The Slovak parliament is preparing a law to regulate the arms trade which will reduce the number of firms licensed to export weapons from around 100 to about six, a senior parliamentarian said on Wednesday.

Vitazoslav Moric, a member of the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the ruling coalition, said at the opening of an international arms fair that the state must take "strong measures" to protect its interests.

"We are preparing a law on the regulation of arms sales, which will drastically limit the number of state-licensed dealers," said Moric, who is also general manager of the state-controlled arms dealer Armex.
Industry sources said, however, that a cut in the number of licences would not mean a slowdown in arms production.

The four-day International Defence Equipment Exhibition is aimed at boosting Slovakia's ailing arms industry, which is suffering from the results of a virtual halt in production in the early 1990s following the collapse of communism.
"We hope this exhibition will revive contacts we had in the past and develop them in the future," said Julius Toth, general director of arms holding company DMD.
Toth said the new strategy of Slovakia's arms industry was to concentrate on a limited number of products, rather than previous efforts to produce all types of weapon systems.

"We shall not go back to producing everything, it is better to buy limited amounts of materials than to develop them," he said. "We are strong in many fields, such as gun and tank production, and will seek new outlets abroad," he added.
